title: Nonlinear Landau-Zener Tunneling with Heat-Bath Colored Noise
abstract: In this work, we investigate the influence of colored noise originating from a heat bath on nonlinear Landau-Zener (LZ) tunneling. The nonlinearity might arise intrinsically from many-body mean-field atomic self-interactions or Kerr nonlinearities in optical systems. Contrary to the well-established picture of thermally enhanced quantum tunneling within the linear LZ paradigm, ensemble statistics of our numerical simulations demonstrate that nonlinearity can give rise to thermally suppressed LZ tunneling: the tunneling probability of the nonlinear LZ system decreases as the amplitude of the colored noise increases beyond a critical value. Analytically, the Wiener-Hermite expansion facilitates elucidation of the intrinsic mechanism accounting for the nonmonotonic dependence of tunneling probability on noise amplitude. We compare these behaviors with stochastic resonance responses and clarify that the two phenomena stem from distinct physical mechanisms. In addition, we obtain approximate solutions in the weak- and strong-noise limits and discuss the implications of our theory.
summary: This paper analyzes nonlinear Landau-Zener tunneling when subjected to heat-bath induced colored noise. It demonstrates that the system's tunneling probability does not simply increase with noise but instead shows a nonmonotonic dependence, peaking at an intermediate noise level due to nonlinearity. The findings clarify this mechanism and distinguish it from other noise-induced phenomena.
main_problem: The study investigates how colored noise originating from a heat bath affects nonlinear Landau-Zener (LZ) tunneling dynamics.
main_result: Unlike the linear case where tunneling increases monotonically with noise, nonlinearity causes the tunneling probability to exhibit nonmonotonic behavior: it peaks at a finite noise amplitude before decreasing.
method: The analysis employs numerical simulations of the stochastic Schrödinger equation and utilizes the Wiener-Hermite expansion for analytical elucidation.
model_or_system: The model is a nonlinear LZ system coupled to a bosonic heat bath, applicable to systems like BECs or Kerr nonlinear optical waveguides. The dynamics are governed by an effective stochastic Hamiltonian derived from the coupling to the bath.
key_observables: Ensemble-averaged tunneling probability ($ ar{P}$), which depends on noise amplitude and nonlinearity strength.
important_parameters: Noise amplitude ($D$), nonlinear parameter ($c$), noise correlation time ($\gamma$), and sweep rate ($\alpha$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the Markovian approximation for the bath coupling and uses approximations like moment-closure or specific limits (weak/strong noise).
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the nonmonotonic dependence of $ ar{P}$ vs. $D$ for nonlinear systems, contrasting it with the monotonic behavior of linear systems.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the model Hamiltonian and dynamics under colored noise, uses numerical simulations to observe nonmonotonicity, and employs analytical tools like the Wiener-Hermite expansion to explain the underlying physical mechanism distinguishing this from stochastic resonance.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant as it tackles open quantum systems dynamics (LZ tunneling) under realistic colored noise sources, providing a detailed understanding of how nonlinearity fundamentally alters thermal excitation mechanisms compared to standard linear models.
